deviations_from_the_spec: Location: the brief puts the scripts at tcb/<name>.mjs, but CONTRACT §0 and the tests already written (tcb/test/*.test.mjs import '../scripts/<name>.mjs') expect tcb/scripts/. The scripts import './lib.mjs' and './admit.mjs' by relative path, so they work in either place as long as lib.mjs sits next to them. Someone still has to move them into tcb/scripts/.

Paths: lib.paths(root) is used only for attempt(task, e), as a fallback after the folder the fence recorded in the row. The other §2 paths (run/watcher.json, run/stop-sample/, store/commits/<task>.<step>.json, completeness/gate.json and cut-<sha12>.md, review-in/, sealed/plants/, .snapshots/text/, store/witness.jsonl, store/status/card_status.jsonl, plan/our-work/) are written out with path.join, because the contract does not fix the key names of paths().

The contract does not settle this one: replace start must call gatherFacts 'inside its lock', but §2.1 forbids parsing transcripts under the lock. So gatherFacts takes extra optional parameters {spentOf, table, cache}. replace works out every attempt's spend before it takes the lock and passes it in. Inside the lock, only lib.slotCount may look at whether transcript files exist.

admit.mjs exports more than decide and gatherFacts: also attemptTranscriptFiles, spendOfFiles, attemptSpend, spentOfRows and thresholdReader. replace.mjs imports them (same unit, decision 19). stop.mjs keeps its own copy of the transcript-collection helper, because it may not import admit.

gatherFacts also returns `unreadable` (fact files that are missing, unparseable or have the wrong schema_version: completeness/gate.json, run/coord.json). check exits 2 when these are present or when the only refusal is slots-unknown. Without --task, check exits 2 if no candidate can be admitted and at least one refusal is of that kind; otherwise 6.

decide accepts thresholds either as plain values or as {value, gate}. It takes the gate flags from thresholds.isGate, whether that is an object or a function with properties, and treats a non-null value as a gate by default. It adds `param-missing` when N_max, peak_mb or reserve_mb is absent. A null freeMb refuses with `memory` (fail-safe). slots-full compares against min(N_max, N_ceiling, 3).

stop-sample: the file is named <task>-e<k>.json after the target attempt k, not the row's epoch, which is what the tests expect. It is written as {schema_version:1, task, epoch:k, target:k, tick, sizes}; target is an integer.

READY check (replace fence): the briefs tell sessions to write READY without schema_version. So a READY with no schema_version is first validated directly with lib.validate(loadSchema('ready')), then once more with schema_version:1 added. Only a READY that does carry a schema_version goes through the strict checkFormat path.

Briefs: the roles child-reviewing and control fall back to tcb/briefs/child.md (spec/briefs.md says the child brief serves them). A role with no brief at all, such as canary, exits 2 missing. Placeholder values are: folder = the absolute attempt path with forward slashes; todo_json = the uncovered id list; checkpoint_json = {committed: [ids], prefix: [relpaths]}; must_read_json = the protocol's must_read list (or [] when there is no field).

Settings: {root} and {attempt} are filled in with forward slashes. Every value is JSON-string-escaped (so node's backslashes come out as \\), and the result must parse as JSON, or the script exits 2 settings-placeholder.

Incidents: replace writes an incident {class: refusal} on every exit 1, which includes the `limit` path where the fence is applied, and on exits 5 and 6. Exit 3 (except run-from-attempt and ledger-broken) gets the tamper form. stop writes refusal on exit 1 (including stop-unconfirmed) and not-run on exit 2, except `no-watcher`: step 3 of the spec says nothing is written there.

Both replace and stop also run lib.checkCe once, read-only, before any other refusal. A stale coordinator therefore gets 64 even on paths that write nothing (stop verify `waiting`, a fence refused for `no-tick`). The check inside withRunLock still guards every write.

replace fence --dry-run cannot call lib.fence, which writes. So a local predictFence works out the exit from the §3.6 rows: epoch 65, wrong-step 65, ready-wins 5, hmax 1, limit 1, the no-attempt cut/drop. This is a prediction only; the real run always goes through lib.fence.

In mapper inputs, lib.currentDesign returns no stpa or fmea ids. replace picks them itself with gate.mjs's rule: a committed design-check row of that role, its commit-record output of that kind, cut_sha equal to the current cut, and the highest `commit` ledger seq.

Checkpoint prefixes: when two earlier attempts both have the same relpath with different bytes, the later attempt's bytes win and the relpath is listed in result.checkpoint.conflicts. `mismatched` is the union, as a list of posix relpath strings. An `s_` id is looked for in committed outputs (id and canonical text), not in prefixes from untrusted staging.
The manifest carries schema_version:1, because §3 says every object carries one even though §3.5 does not list it. `inputs` leaves out in/manifest.json itself.
bind reads the first cwd of the session's transcript before taking the lock, using its own small chunked reader, not parseTranscript. The comparison with the attempt folder is case-folded.
lib_change_requests: currentDesign(root) should also return stpa_id/stpa_sha and fmea_id/fmea_sha, picked by the same 'highest commit ledger seq' rule. replace and gate would then share that rule instead of each re-implementing it.
withRunLock(root, {script, ce, proc, now, retries}) should pass `retries` on to acquireLock. The scripts pass threshold lock_retries this way, and the exit-75 tests set it to 3.
Export TcbError with the constructor (code, exit, detail). The scripts fall back to a plain Error with code, exit and detail when it is missing, so runMain should recognise either form.

runMain should take mode and dry_run for the §1.3 line from the object fn returns ({exit, result, reasons, mode, dry_run}) or from ctx.mode / ctx.dryRun, which the scripts set before parseArgs. That way an early usage error still prints the right mode and dry_run.

Fix the key names of paths(root) in the contract, for example watcher, stopSample(task, e), commitRecord(task, step), gate, cutFile(sha), reviewIn(task), snapshotText(sha), plants(task), so scripts can stop spelling these paths themselves.
Add a small removeFile(path) helper with the Windows-sharing retries. stop.mjs currently removes its sample with fs.rmSync and only reports a failure on stderr.

The [ready] schema should not require schema_version, because the briefs have sessions write {kind, task, epoch, step} without one. Otherwise the briefs need to add it. As things stand, checkFormat would reject every real READY marker.
The [stop-sample] schema should give `target` as an integer (the target attempt's epoch) and `epoch` as that same k, which is what stop.mjs writes and the tests expect.
not_testable_without_the_app: replace: whether the rendered .claude/settings.json (PreToolUse hook running guard-hook.mjs) and .claude/agents/<type>.md actually bind a session started in the attempt folder (CONTRACT §7 item 3).

replace bind: whether a real session's transcript `cwd` (first record) equals the attempt folder named in bind, and whether projectDirName matches the harness's folder naming, so the wrong-folder check sees real transcripts (§7 item 7).

admit, and replace start through it: whether lib.attemptProcesses finds a real session's processes (a claude.exe command line naming its folder or session id), so `live` and `pending` count real children (§7 item 4).
admit: whether peak_mb = 1200 matches the memory a real session takes. It is a guess until measured, so the memory refusal can only be calibrated in the app.

stop request/verify: whether the coordinator's own stop really ends a real session's turn and its helpers, and whether a real claude.exe command line names the folder or session id, so that real orphans show up in `survivors` (§7 item 4).
stop verify: real transcript flush timing within stop_verify_deltas watcher ticks, i.e. whether a still-running session always shows growth within 2 ticks.
fence host class: whether lib.realProc boot() (LastBootUpTime) changes across a real shutdown on this PC. With Fast Startup on it may not, and the failure would be charged.
open_points: tcb/lib.mjs did not exist while I worked, so none of the three scripts has been run end to end. The only check was decide() against a stub reservation(), using literal facts copied from the admit tests: T1, T3/T4, T6, T7, T8 and T10 came out as expected. All three files pass node --check.

The shipped tcb/thresholds.json (owned by the briefs unit) does not yet match CONTRACT §3.20. It lacks lock_retries, proc_exe, user_files, child_prefix_tokens, review_reserve_tokens, sleep_gap_ms and others; it still has audit_coord_turn_factor; its tcb_paths_protected lacks '.git/'; and the B_tokens/r_tokens unit text says 'null = admission refused', which contradicts decision 39. The scripts default lock_retries to 300 and user_files to [], and they require proc_exe (param-missing 2 when absent).

replace and stop create lib.realProc({exe: proc_exe}) for the lock's selfInfo. In stop's T13, proc_exe points at a missing file, so the not-run incident can only be written if lib.acquireLock can still take the lock when selfInfo's PowerShell call fails (pid only, start_time null). This depends on how lib is built.

Spec ambiguity I settled one way: on the limit path (exit 1, fence applied), replace also writes an incident line. If the orchestrator wants incidents only for refusals that changed nothing, remove that one line in modeFence.
Spec ambiguity: stop exit 1 `stop-unconfirmed` also writes an incident {class: refusal}, following the literal 'incident on exits 1 and 2'. The tests do not count incidents in that case.
